title: NDFT: Accelerating Density Functional Theory Calculations via Hardware/Software Co-Design on Near-Data Computing System
problem: Linear-response time-dependent DFT (LR-TDDFT) is memory-bound with constant data movement between host and heterogeneous accelerators (GPU, FPGA, Sunway), creating substantial data movement overhead that dominates compute-optimized kernels.
motivation: Excited-state property prediction is critical in materials science and quantum chemistry, but existing heterogeneous acceleration leaves memory as the primary bottleneck, wasting compute resources and power.
method: NDFT reduces data-movement bottlenecks by using near-data processing—executing calculations on processing units built into the memory system instead of shipping data to distant accelerators. It splits the quantum chemistry calculation into stages and assigns each to whichever processor (CPU or on-chip unit) is most efficient for that task. The hardware and software are then co-designed: the chip's architecture and the algorithms are redesigned together, rather than separately, to further squeeze out data movement and reduce delays.
key_novelty: This is the first near-data processing system for quantum chemistry calculations, dividing computational work between the CPU and on-chip processing units to minimize long-distance data movement, and achieving 5.2× speedup over pure CPU and 2.5× over GPU.
contributions: Novel task partitioning and scheduling mechanism for LR-TDDFT across CPU-NDP system.
Hardware/software co-optimization of critical LR-TDDFT kernels on near-data processing.
5.2x speedup vs CPU, 2.5x vs GPU on large physical systems with reduced data movement.
primary_theme: memory-bound HPC acceleration via near-data processing
